Thought: Let me analyze each option:

A. Cadmium compounds - Cadmium is a heavy metal and is generally toxic. It's not commonly used as a fungicide in agriculture due to its toxicity to humans and the environment.

B. Mercury compounds - While mercury compounds were historically used as fungicides, they have been largely banned worldwide due to their high toxicity and environmental persistence.

C. Sulfur - Sulfur is one of the oldest known fungicides and is still widely used today in crop protection. It's effective against powdery mildew and other fungal diseases and is even allowed in organic farming.

D. Triazoles - Triazoles are a class of synthetic fungicides that are commonly used in modern agriculture. They work by inhibiting ergosterol biosynthesis in fungi.

Based on my knowledge, both sulfur (C) and triazoles (D) are used as fungicides in crop protection. Cadmium and mercury compounds are not typically used as fungicides in modern agriculture due to their toxicity.
